title: Part over Whole
description: Put a part over its whole, both in one unit, and make it a per cent with the bracketed rule, the % sign last.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Write one number as a per cent of another by putting the part over the whole, with the bracketed rule, both amounts in one unit first, and tell the matches not won from the matches counted against a team.
writeup.look: A whole bar labelled 100% over a part bar at the same scale. The fraction card and the Rule button stand beside them, with the Unit fact card, and on the last phase a row of match tiles.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Part over Whole' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the per cent of the whole bar that the part covers. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The whole bar lies at x 110, y 240, 900 long and 70 tall, labelled Whole and 100%, and the part bar lies under it at x 110, y 330, drawn to the same scale in deep blue, labelled Part. The fraction card stands at x 110, y 440 with the Times buttons in a row beside it; when both terms grow, the words Both terms light vermilion. The Rule button builds its brackets at x 110, y 560, the times one hundred step vermilion and the % sign in ink after the closing bracket, and the per cent reached is green. The Unit fact card stands at x 700, y 440 and rewrites an amount in violet. For several parts of one whole, each part takes its own band on the whole bar with its per cent written on it. On the fourth phase the match tiles, each 70 by 70, lie in a row at y 250 and are dragged into a Won row at y 400 and a Not won row at y 520, the Not won row rose; a tile turned over shows the word Draw. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with a fraction bar key, a point key, a % key and unit keys. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the tools of this chapter share them. The part the question gives, as shaded cells, a fraction, a decimal or an amount, is deep blue, labelled Given. The per cent, fraction or decimal the working reaches, and what is left after a part is used, is green, labelled Answer or Left. Both terms multiplied or divided by one number, and the times one hundred step before the % sign, are vermilion, labelled Both terms or Times 100. A unit fact that puts two amounts in one unit is violet, labelled Unit fact. The part used, taken away or not won is rose, labelled Used or Not won. The step, cell or number being worked on now is amber. A zero holding a place open inside a decimal is grey, labelled Place holder, and nothing else on the stage is ever grey. An unshaded cell of a whole stays warm white inside its near-black outline, the % sign is near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength rather than turning grey. Chrome never borrows one of them, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The bars show the last part against its whole, the bracketed line under them, and the unit fact that was used.

phases.win: the bands read 56%, 32% and 12%, and together they fill the whole bar
phases.does: taps Part over whole for each colour, grows each fraction to hundredths, and reads the bands
phases.goal: the part over the whole, made into hundredths, is the per cent. The parts of one whole make 100% together
phases.says: Name the whole first. Then put each part over it.
phases.check: Away from the screen: some of your class walked to school and the rest did not. What do their two per cents make together?
phases.feels: the coloured bands filling the whole bar exactly
phases.hands: Count a group in the class and the children in it who walked to school. Write the walkers over the whole group, make the denominator one hundred, and check that the walkers and the others make one hundred per cent.
phases.tries: First rung: name the whole and count it. Second rung: put one part over it. Third rung: the same task with a whole that goes into one hundred, before the question's own returns.

wrong.why: the other parts are the ones sitting next to it
wrong.move: puts the part over the other parts instead of over the whole
wrong.screen: the whole bar lights end to end in amber and its count is written under it, beside the child's fraction, with the part's band kept

wrong.why: a slip in one band's per cent is easy to miss
wrong.move: types band per cents that add to more than the whole
wrong.screen: the bands are laid end to end along the whole bar, and the one that runs past its end is lit amber

phases.screen: a whole bar of 25 beads with 14 red, 8 blue and 3 yellow, and the fraction card blank
phases.soWhat: the part over the whole, made into hundredths, is the per cent, and the parts of one whole make one hundred per cent together

phases.win: the line reads (18/30 x 100)% = 60%, with the % sign after the closing bracket
phases.does: taps Rule, places each number in the formula, and places the % sign last
phases.goal: the first number over the second, times 100, in brackets, then the % sign
phases.says: First number over the second, times a hundred. The sign goes after the brackets.
phases.check: Away from the screen: which number goes on top when you ask what per cent one number is of another?
phases.feels: the brackets closing, and the sign landing last
phases.hands: Write the rule on a card with empty boxes: the first number over the second, times one hundred, in brackets, then the % sign. Fill the boxes for a pair of numbers.
phases.tries: First rung: place the first number on top. Second rung: place the second under it and add times one hundred. Third rung: the same task with a second number that goes into one hundred, before the question's own returns.

wrong.why: the bigger number often comes first in the child's head
wrong.move: puts the second number over the first
wrong.screen: the part bar and the whole bar are drawn for the child's order, the part longer than its whole, lit amber

wrong.why: the sign seems to belong to the hundred
wrong.move: writes the % sign inside the brackets
wrong.screen: the sign tile goes back to its tray, and the closing bracket is lit amber until the sign is placed after it

phases.screen: the question card asking what per cent 18 is of 30, and the Rule button lit
phases.soWhat: the first number over the second, times one hundred, in brackets, then the % sign

phases.win: the whole bar reads 2000 g in violet, and the card reads 600 g is 30% of 2000 g
phases.does: picks the Unit fact card, watches the whole relabel in grams, and finds the per cent
phases.goal: first write both amounts in the same unit, and state the unit fact used
phases.says: Grams and kilograms do not match yet. Which unit fact helps?
phases.check: Away from the screen: what is the unit fact that joins metres and centimetres?
phases.feels: two amounts in two units becoming one bar in one unit
phases.hands: Weigh something small in grams and something bigger in kilograms, or measure in centimetres and metres. Write the unit fact, rewrite one amount, then find the per cent.
phases.tries: First rung: pick the unit fact card. Second rung: rewrite one amount and read both. Third rung: the same task with a whole of one unit, before the question's own returns.

wrong.why: both numbers are right there, and the units seem like labels
wrong.move: puts the two numbers over each other without changing a unit
wrong.screen: the part bar is drawn to the child's numbers, far longer than the whole, and the two unit words are lit amber

wrong.why: several facts on the card list look alike
wrong.move: picks a unit fact that does not join the two units
wrong.screen: the chosen fact is written in violet beside the bar, and the bar redraws to it, so the part is seen not to fit

phases.screen: a whole bar of 2 kg and a part bar of 600 g, too long to lie against it
phases.soWhat: first write both amounts in the same unit, and state the unit fact used

phases.win: nine tiles in the Not won row, and the card reads 30% not won
phases.does: drags the tiles that were not won into their own row, and finds that row's per cent
phases.goal: not won is the whole take away the matches won, and it counts as lost only when every match was either won or lost
phases.says: Which matches were not won? Is a draw a match the team did not win?
phases.check: Away from the screen: a team won some matches and drew some. Is every match it did not win a loss?
phases.feels: a draw tile flipping over and staying in the Not won row
phases.hands: Lay out cards for a team's matches, some marked won and some marked draw. Sort them into won and not won, and find the per cent not won.
phases.tries: First rung: count the tiles in the Won row. Second rung: count the tiles in the Not won row. Third rung: the same task with a row that has no draw, before the question's own returns.

wrong.why: the won tiles are the marked ones, so their per cent comes first
wrong.move: gives the per cent won when the question asks for not won
wrong.screen: the Not won row is lit rose and counted tile by tile, beside the Won row's count

wrong.why: a match not won feels like a match that went badly
wrong.move: counts every Not won tile as a loss, draws too
wrong.screen: the draw tile turns over to show the word Draw and stays in the Not won row, set apart from the others and lit amber

phases.screen: thirty match tiles, twenty-one of them marked won and three turned to show a draw
phases.soWhat: not won is the whole take away the matches won, and it counts as lost only when every match was either won or lost

writeup.delight: On the third phase, the moment the Unit fact card is dropped, the whole bar's label rewrites itself in violet, and the part bar shrinks to its true length and settles against the whole with a soft click.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet tapped. On the first phase the whole bar holds beads of several colours, with the fraction card blank. On the second the question card asks what per cent one number is of another, with the Rule button lit. On the third the whole bar and the part bar carry amounts in two units, the part bar too long to lie against the whole. On the fourth a row of match tiles waits, some marked won and some turned to show a draw. One thing moves, once: the first control the phase needs gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: A part and a whole of the child's own, in one unit or two, and any row of match tiles. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on parts of a whole, the bracketed rule, amounts in two units, and matches not won.

Name the whole first. Then put each part over it.
First number over the second, times a hundred. The sign goes after the brackets.
Grams and kilograms do not match yet. Which unit fact helps?
Which matches were not won? Is a draw a match the team did not win?

Free play. Lay any part against any whole.
Name the whole again, then put the part over it.
Every part found its per cent against its own whole.

observations.why: every part of the whole is counted once, and nothing is left out.
observations.soWhat: the parts of one whole, as per cents, make one hundred per cent together.
observations.observe: The coloured bands of one whole always filled the whole bar.

observations.why: the sign names the whole product.
observations.soWhat: the rule is the first number over the second, times one hundred, in brackets, then the % sign.
observations.observe: The % sign could only be placed after the closing bracket.

observations.why: grams and kilograms count different sizes of amount.
observations.soWhat: first write both amounts in the same unit, and say the unit fact used.
observations.observe: The bars would not lie against each other until both amounts were in one unit.

observations.why: a draw is not a win, and it is not a loss either.
observations.soWhat: not won counts as lost only when every match was either won or lost.
observations.observe: A tile turned to show a draw stayed in the Not won row.

phases.screen: a whole bar of 25 beads with 14 red, 8 blue and 3 yellow, and the fraction card blank
phases.win: the bands read 56%, 32% and 12%, and together they fill the whole bar
phases.traceback: The whole bar lights amber, the part goes over all of it, both terms grow until the bottom is 100, and the per cent is written.
ladder: The whole is all 50 plants, not just the roses and lilies.
Put the 7 red beads over all 10 beads.
The white cups go over all 60 cups.
Put the part over the whole, then make the bottom 100.
When the bottom is 100, the top number is the per cent.

phases.screen: the question card asking what per cent 18 is of 30, and the Rule button lit
phases.win: the line reads (18/30 x 100)% = 60%, with the % sign after the closing bracket
phases.traceback: The part bar lights amber, the rule is written whole with the first number over the second, and the per cent is written after it.
ladder: Write 26 over 40 inside the brackets.
Put 9 over 25, since 9 is the first number.
Put 27 on top and 30 below, then times 100.
Write the first number over the second, times 100, inside the brackets.
Times the top number by 100, then divide by the bottom number.

phases.screen: a whole bar of 2 kg and a part bar of 600 g, too long to lie against it
phases.win: the whole bar reads 2000 g in violet, and the card reads 600 g is 30% of 2000 g
phases.traceback: The unit fact rewrites the whole in violet, the part bar settles at its true length, and the part over the whole is made into hundredths.
ladder: Change 5 litres into millilitres before you divide.
Change 2 m into centimetres first.
Turn 3 kg into grams, then put 360 g over it.
Change the whole into the part's unit, then put the part over it.
Do the same to the top and the bottom until the bottom is 100.

phases.screen: thirty match tiles, twenty-one of them marked won and three turned to show a draw
phases.win: nine tiles in the Not won row, and the card reads 30% not won
phases.traceback: The tiles sort into Won and Not won, the Not won row lights and is counted, and its count over all the matches is made into hundredths.
ladder: Not won is all 25 take away the 17 won.
First count the matches this team did not win.
Count the matches not won, then put them over 50.
Put the matches not won over all the matches played.
Make the bottom 100 by doing the same to the top and the bottom.
No whole number times 60 makes 100, so divide the top and the bottom by 3 first.
After dividing by 3, times the top and the bottom by 5.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: The whole bar lights amber, the part goes over all of it, both terms grow until the bottom is 100, and the per cent is written.
Phase 2: The part bar lights amber, the rule is written whole with the first number over the second, and the per cent is written after it.
Phase 3: The unit fact rewrites the whole in violet, the part bar settles at its true length, and the part over the whole is made into hundredths.
Phase 4: The tiles sort into Won and Not won, the Not won row lights and is counted, and its count over all the matches is made into hundredths.

voice.opening: A whole, and a part to lay against it.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play. Lay any part against any whole.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: Every part found its per cent against its own whole.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

items.planQuestion: A garden bed has 50 plants: 23 marigolds, 19 roses and 8 lilies. What per cent of the plants are marigolds?

question.en: Of 50 plants, 23 are marigolds, 19 roses, 8 lilies: what per cent are marigolds?

items.planQuestion: A box has 10 beads: 7 red and 3 blue. What per cent of the beads are red?

question.en: A box has 10 beads, 7 red and 3 blue: what per cent of the beads are red?

items.planQuestion: A tray has 60 cups: 27 white and 33 green. What per cent of the cups are white?

question.en: A tray has 60 cups, 27 white and 33 green: what per cent of the cups are white?

items.planQuestion: Use the rule with brackets to find what per cent 27 is of 30.

question.en: Use the rule with brackets to find what per cent 27 is of 30.

items.planQuestion: What per cent of 5 litres is 1200 mL?

question.en: What per cent of 5 litres is 1,200 mL?

items.planQuestion: What per cent of 1 m is 40 cm?

question.en: What per cent of 2 m is 40 cm?

items.planAnswer: 40%. 1 m = 100 cm, and 40 cm out of 100 cm is 40%

items.planQuestion: What per cent of 3 kg is 360 g?

question.en: What per cent of 3 kg is 360 g?

items.planQuestion: A team played 25 matches and won 17. What per cent of its matches did it not win?

question.en: A team played 25 matches and won 17: what per cent did it not win?

items.planQuestion: A team played 20 matches and won 16. What per cent of its matches did it not win?

question.en: Another team won 15 of its 20 matches: what per cent did it not win?

ask.en: Not won as a per cent?

items.planAnswer: 20%. 4 of the 20 matches were not won, and 4 of 20 is 20%

items.planQuestion: A team played 50 matches and won 31, and every match was either won or lost. What per cent of its matches did it lose?

question.en: Every match was won or lost: a team won 31 of 50, so what per cent did it lose?

items.planAnswer: 38%. 50 - 31 = 19 matches were not won, and since every match was either won or lost, 19 were lost: 19/50 = 38/100, which is 38%

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.

onProgress.done: questions right so far in this phase

hostContract.emits: every event is dispatched on window and, when framed, posted to window.parent as { type: 'event', name, detail }
